react-native-markdown-display builds markdown-it with typographer only, and linkify is off by default, so linkify-it never scans a member's text.
Both slow paths are in linkify, which react-native-markdown-display never turns on.

The smart-quotes slowdown grows with the length of the text. The one mount, EssayBody, renders only text cut by capMarkdownForRender to the 25,000 characters an essay is written under, where the worst case measures under half a second (src/utils/markdownSafety.ts).
The slowdown needs a pattern longer than 50,000 characters. The one mount, EssayBody, renders only text cut by capMarkdownForRender to 25,000.

Smart quotes with unmatched closers grow with the length of the text. Measured on this markdown-it 10.0.0 built as the library builds it (typographer on): 56 ms at the 25,000 characters capMarkdownForRender cuts EssayBody's text to (34 ms with the quotes reversed), 2.3 s only at 100,000, which the cap never lets through. That is under the smart-quotes case GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq already measured at the cap.

The slowdown is in inline HTML, which runs only with html on. react-native-markdown-display builds markdown-it with typographer alone (html off by default), and no mount passes a parser of its own; measured with html off, the payload stays linear (7 ms at 25,000 characters).
